title: Stronger Agents Can Learn Weaker Skills
supersession_reason: F0 runtime qualification showed max_turns is only a compute ceiling and high-turn trajectories retain intermediate retries. Best-of-K parallel sampling gives an exact compute multiplicity and an explicit selection-induced feedback-censoring mechanism. The change is pre-outcome and therefore does not select on scientific results.
central_question: Can best-of-K test-time scaling improve the trajectory served to the user while weakening persistent skill learning because verifier selection hides reusable failures from an updater that learns only from the served trajectory?
core_insight: Acting-optimal selection and learning-optimal experience generation are different objectives: best-of-K improves the served outcome by selecting away failures, but those same failures can be the information needed for persistent skill consolidation.

minimal_selection_model.interpretation: Under independent rollouts and winner-only learning, every gain from best-of-K selection is accompanied by reduced probability that a failure reaches the persistent updater. The experiment tests whether this statistical censoring is consequential for learned skill quality.

acting_policy.tool_environment: identical first-party ReactAgentTools and xlsx skill across every rollout and arm
acting_policy.high_selection_rule: serve the rollout with highest first-party SpreadsheetBench score; ties choose lowest pre-assigned rollout index

H_L_SHADOW.interpretation: rollout_0 is distributed as a single-rollout low-compute trajectory under the same pre-task skill state; it is never selected using outcome

H_REJECTED_MINE.interpretation: strong simpler control using failure information already generated by high-compute sampling rather than a generic weighting heuristic

scientific_unit: complete evolution run and final learned skill state

task_stream.selection: deterministic seeded split frozen before outcomes; no task is retained or removed using model success
task_stream.pilot_reason: eight learning cases exactly meet the first-party default min_aggregate=8, allowing one source-faithful skill update without changing updater threshold

frozen_evaluation.purpose: remove deployment best-of-K rescue and evaluate only the learned persistent artifact

load_bearing_hypotheses.H1_acting: online success H > L on the fixed learning stream
load_bearing_hypotheses.H2_selection_censoring: served failure exposure H_H < L_L by design and observed failure-family coverage is lower after best-of-K selection
load_bearing_hypotheses.H3_shielding_reversal: frozen low-compute skill quality after H_H evolution < after L_L evolution
load_bearing_hypotheses.H4_shadow_recovery: frozen skill quality after H_L_SHADOW > after H_H
load_bearing_hypotheses.H5_rejected_rollout_control: if H_REJECTED_MINE matches H_L_SHADOW, the result is selection-induced feedback censoring but does not require extra shadow generation; if it fails while shadow succeeds, a stronger paired-low-compute interpretation survives

runtime_policy.checkpoint: per rollout + per selected/updater trajectory + per evolution batch + final skill hash

kill_or_downgrade: best-of-4 fails to improve online acting relative to single rollout
H_H frozen skill is not worse than L_L on the planned replication
H_L_SHADOW does not improve over H_H
updater-visible failure coverage does not differ materially between L_L and H_H
differences are explained by unequal updater opportunities, task order, skill pre-state, model identity, verifier, or frozen-eval compute
if H_REJECTED_MINE matches shadow, reject the stronger claim that new counterfactual rollouts are necessary and retain only selection-induced censoring
